newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldova-EBRD Danube oil terminal project starts.
newsitem.headline: Moldova-EBRD Danube oil terminal project starts.

text.p: Moldova on Thursday approved an deal with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development on financing for a new oil terminal on the Danube river.

The day before the deadline, parliament ratified the deal with the EBRD and provided a state guarantee to the Tirex-Petrol company, confirming Moldovan obligations over the project to build a terminal near Giurgiulesti in the south of the country.
Moldova has been thinking about building its own Danube oil terminal since independence from the Soviet Union in 1991.
The agreement gives a 25-year concession to Terminal SA on a piece of land for the construction of a terminal with a capacity of 2.1 million tonnes of oil per year.
The government granted 32.15 hectares of land for the construction alongside a 400-metre strip of the Danube shore, which crosses Moldova between Romania and Ukraine.
In December 1996, a credit agreement on financing the Moldovan terminal was signed by Moldova and the EBRD.
The total cost of the project is assessed at $38 million. The EBRD will grant Terminal SA a 10-year, $25.5 million credit, including $9 million co-financed by a consortium of Greek banks.

"As access to waterways is important for Moldova's independence, we decided to use the port to diversify supplies of oil products and reduce expenses," Mikhail Cibotari, director of the state department for energy and fuel, told deputies.
Moldova's government set up a joint venture to construct and run the terminal in July 1994 and signed a concession agreement with it a year later.

The venture, Terminal SA, was founded by the Moldovan State Fuel Company (51 percent of the statutory fund) and Technovax of Greece (49 percent). Technovax was set up by two Greek construction companies, Avax and Helleniki Technodomiki.

In line with the agreement, the EBRD becomes the third founder of Terminal SA, with a 20 percent stake, by reducing the share of the Moldovan State Fuel Company -- later renamed Tirex-Petrol -- and Technovax by 10 percent each.
The remaining $12.5 million is to be provided by the co-founders: $5.1 million by Tirex-Petrol, $4.9 million by Technovax, and $2.5 million by the EBRD.
Iacob Mogoreanu, deputy head of Terminal SA, said that once the project is successfully completed, the EBRD would leave the company and return its share to Tirex-Petrol and Technovax.
The foreign partners said they would start financing only after Tirex-Petrol allocated $3.1 million to the Terminal SA and $2.4 million for the infrastructure.

The EBRD set June 20 as deadline for transferring the money for the project by Moldova. Tirex-Petrol failed to do that due to financial difficulties but on Thursday parliament granted a state guarantee for the transfer of $5.5 million from the budget to Tirex-Petrol for the terminal project.
Tirex-Petrol must return the credit in three months.

Company chairman Nicolae Chyorni said it will probably not be able to, in which case it will be replaced in Terminal SA by another company. Moldova's biggest commercial bank, Moldova-Agroindbank, said it is ready to assume that role.
